records.detail: Cassandra CQL in the KG, row, config, IAM, knowledge and library stores: values are bound (?), only keyspace/table identifiers are f-strings, built from names passed through sanitize_name (re.sub [^a-zA-Z0-9_]).
Same CQL sites plus the FTS5 keyword index, whose table name is kw_<ws>_<coll> with [^A-Za-z0-9_-] stripped and then quoted; the MATCH text is bound.
Client libraries and the MCP server derive ws:// from an http:// gateway URL and wss:// from https:// (socket_client.py:108-114): the scheme follows the operator's configured URL.
Eight Containerfiles run as root. Defence in depth for a multi-container deployment; no finding on its own.
First-party and docker actions pinned by tag in release, build, PR and CLA workflows.

build-container.yaml is workflow_call only; its inputs come from release.yaml, which runs on maintainer tag pushes (v*) and workflow_dispatch. No external contributor controls the interpolated values.
processing.py loads the operator's own process-group definition file given on the command line with yaml.Loader; no request data. SafeLoader would be the tidier choice.
dev-tools/proc-group YAML: the access/secret key pair of a local Garage object store at localhost:3900 for development runs.
tests/unit/test_agent/test_mcp_tool_auth.py: the public jwt.io example token used to test special characters in auth headers.
Two in dev-tools/library_client.py (developer script, not packaged); one in the Pulsar backend calling the operator-configured Pulsar admin URL.
docs/api.html, the generated API reference page; not served by the product.
importlib on module paths from the operator's processor-group and bootstrap configuration files; no request data reaches them.
RabbitMQ backend defaults to guest/guest, RabbitMQ's own local default; overridden by configuration.
Performance lint in the cloze model service, not a security issue.
sparql/expressions.py implements the SPARQL 1.1 SHA1() function; the standard mandates it, so 'use a stronger hash' would break query compliance.
importlib.resources usage flagged for Python 3.7; the packages require a modern Python.

Hand review; no tool rule covers them. Two first-party findings (one High, one Medium), each reported privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting on 2026-11-21, one report per finding. Detail withheld until a fix ships.
